title: The women who funded him (Luke 8:1–3)
hookLine: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others ministered to him of their substance

cards: Here's a question the Gospels rarely stop to answer: who paid for all this? Jesus and twelve men walking from town to town for months, not fishing, not farming, not working for wages.
Somebody bought the bread, the sandals, the oil, a roof when there was one. Most of the time the Gospels skip the budget. Luke doesn't.
In three short verses, tucked between bigger stories, he tells us who kept the whole mission going.

teach.b: Jesus went through the cities and towns preaching the kingdom, Luke says, and the twelve were with him, and certain women. Then he names them. Mary, called Magdalene, out of whom seven devils had gone.
Joanna, wife of Chusa, Herod's steward: married to the man who managed the household of the king who would later mock Jesus. Susanna, about whom we know nothing else at all.
And "many others who ministered unto him of their substance."

teach.h: OF THEIR SUBSTANCE: THEIR OWN MONEY.
teach.b: Their substance means their own money and goods. These women weren't just along for the ride. They were paying for it.
In Greek it's diakoneo, to serve, the same root that gives the Church the word deacon. Now follow these women forward.
Luke says the women who had followed him from Galilee stood at a distance and watched the crucifixion, and saw where he was laid.

teach.h: THE SAME WOMEN AT THE TOMB.
teach.b: On Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene and Joanna are named among the women who found the tomb empty and told the apostles. The ones who funded the road were still there at the end.
In 2016 Pope Francis raised the memorial of Mary Magdalene to a feast, and the decree honored her with an old title: apostle to the apostles.
Many parishes still run on people like Joanna and Susanna, often women, often unnamed: the ones who count the collection, wash the linens, teach the children, bring the casseroles.

how: The Church keeps the feast of Saint Mary Magdalene on July 22, and in many Catholic parishes women carry much of the daily work: catechesis, sacristy care, charity, music and administration.

o: a woman who funded Jesus and was at the empty tomb
a rich widow who gave Jesus a house in Galilee
a disciple's wife who cooked for the twelve

games.q: the women of Luke 8 — tap the pairs.
p: seven devils had gone out of her
out of their own money and goods

s: the Gospels never say how Jesus' mission was paid for
Luke 8:3 says women ministered to him of their substance.
Joanna was married to a man in Herod's household
Joanna disappears from Luke after chapter 8
she's named among the women at the empty tomb in Luke 24:10.

games.q: you're Joanna, married to a steward in Herod's palace. a traveling preacher's group needs money to keep going. what do you do?
o: stay out of it; your husband's job is at stake.
give from your own means and go with them.
send a small gift and stay home.
games.why: Luke names her among the women who traveled with him and ministered of their substance, and she's at the tomb on Easter morning.

practice: Picture the place you belong, a parish, a school, a team, a family, and look for the ones doing the work nobody announces: the one who unlocks the door, makes the coffee, keeps the list, remembers the birthdays.
Pick one, and think of exactly what she gives. If you pray, thank God for her by name.

wordCard.voice: Mary Magdalene. Named first among the women who funded Jesus' mission out of their own means, and stayed to the end, even at the tomb. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: they were serving, from diakoneo, the root of deacon.

carryVoice: Your line: they ministered of their substance. Their own money and goods, spent on the road. That's day four hundred fifty-seven.

sources.q: many others who ministered unto him of their substance
